blocks.text: This Exploratory Data Analysis module has built up a genuinely rich set of tools, one variable at a time in Univariate Analysis, pairs and groups in Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis, precise numbers in Statistical Summary, shape in Distribution Analysis, and joint variability in Covariance Analysis, alongside the dedicated Correlation Analysis and Outlier Detection topics elsewhere in this module. Feature Relationships is the genuine capstone, pulling every one of those individual findings together into one coherent, decision ready view.

This topic covers the two genuinely distinct kinds of relationship worth mapping out, feature to target and feature to feature, why redundant, highly correlated features are worth flagging before modeling begins, how to tell a genuinely real relationship from one that is likely just noise in this particular sample, and why writing all of this down clearly matters before moving into the Feature Engineering module that follows.
1. Recapping the Genuine Toolkit This Module Built

blocks.alt: This module built a toolkit of univariate, bivariate, and multivariate analysis

blocks.text: Univariate analysis established what a single variable genuinely looks like on its own, its center, its spread, its early outlier signals. Bivariate and multivariate analysis extended that into how variables genuinely relate to each other, in pairs and in larger groups, including the humbling reminder from Simpsons paradox that an overall trend can genuinely reverse once a hidden variable is considered.

Statistical summary and distribution analysis added genuine numerical precision and shape to that picture, while covariance and correlation analysis quantified exactly how strongly, and in which direction, pairs of variables genuinely move together, and outlier detection flagged the specific points that do not genuinely fit the rest of the pattern.
2. Two Genuinely Distinct Kinds of Relationship

blocks.alt: A feature relationship can be linear or non-linear

blocks.text: A feature to target relationship asks whether a given variable genuinely helps predict the actual outcome a model will eventually be trained to predict, square footage genuinely relating to price is exactly this kind of relationship, and it is the single most important kind to map, since it directly points toward which variables are worth keeping and developing further.

A feature to feature relationship asks something genuinely different, whether two input variables carry largely the same information as each other, regardless of how either one relates to the target. Both kinds of relationship matter, but they lead to genuinely different decisions, a strong feature to target relationship argues for keeping a variable, while a strong feature to feature relationship between two inputs argues for potentially dropping one of them.

blocks.text: 3. Redundant Features and Multicollinearity

blocks.alt: Two highly correlated features become redundant

blocks.text: When two input variables are genuinely highly correlated with each other, total rooms and the sum of bedrooms plus bathrooms, for instance, they carry largely duplicate information, a pattern often called multicollinearity. Feeding both into certain models, several of the regression algorithms covered later in this course among them, can genuinely make it harder to tell which of the two variables is actually doing the predictive work.

Spotting this kind of redundancy is exactly what the covariance and correlation analysis covered earlier in this module was building toward, a correlation heatmap that shows two input variables strongly correlated with each other, not just with the target, is a genuine, direct signal worth flagging here before modeling begins.

blocks.title: Where this leads next
blocks.content: Flagging redundant, highly correlated input features here is exactly the groundwork the Feature Selection module later in this course builds on directly, deciding precisely which of a set of redundant features to actually keep.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example
A quick correlation check across several features at once, including the target, shows both kinds of relationship side by side in a single small table.

code.content:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100],
    "total_rooms": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    "bedrooms_plus_baths": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    "price": [250000, 310000, 360000, 410000, 460000],
})

print(df.corr()["price"])
print(df["total_rooms"].corr(df["bedrooms_plus_baths"]))

blocks.text: Both square_feet and total_rooms genuinely correlate strongly with price, a useful feature to target signal, while total_rooms and bedrooms_plus_baths correlate almost perfectly with each other, a genuine feature to feature redundancy worth flagging before either one moves forward into modeling.
5. Telling a Real Relationship From Noise

blocks.alt: A real pattern must be told apart from random noise

blocks.text: Not every relationship that shows up in a single dataset is genuinely real, some are simply coincidences specific to that particular sample of data, especially in a genuinely small dataset where a handful of unusual rows can create the appearance of a pattern that would vanish with more data. A genuinely real relationship tends to be consistent, sensible given real domain knowledge, and visible across multiple different views of the data, not just one single chart.

A genuinely useful, practical check is asking whether a found relationship makes real sense given what is actually known about the problem, square footage relating to price makes genuine intuitive sense, while a relationship between a customer id number and price would be a genuinely suspicious coincidence worth double checking rather than trusting outright.

blocks.text: 6. Documenting Findings Before Moving On

blocks.alt: EDA findings get documented before moving on

blocks.text: Everything explored across this entire module, which variables are skewed, which pairs are strongly correlated, which features look redundant, which outliers were found, is genuinely worth writing down clearly before moving into the next module, rather than trusting it to memory. A short, written summary of these findings becomes a genuinely reusable reference, both for future you and for any teammate who later works with the same dataset.

This habit costs genuinely little time relative to the exploration work already done, and it pays off directly the moment a decision made weeks later in the Feature Engineering or Feature Selection modules needs to be justified, having the original exploratory reasoning written down beats trying to re-derive it from scratch.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Keep a short, running list of genuine findings as you explore, not just a mental impression. Which variables are skewed, which pairs are highly correlated, which points looked like outliers, and why each one seemed worth noting.

blocks.text: 7. From Findings to Action

blocks.alt: Findings feed directly into feature engineering

blocks.text: The documented findings from this module genuinely translate directly into concrete decisions for what comes next. A strong feature to target relationship suggests a variable is genuinely worth developing further, perhaps combined with others into a new, more informative feature. A strong feature to feature relationship suggests one of a redundant pair may genuinely be worth dropping rather than keeping both.

A skewed distribution found earlier suggests a transformation may genuinely be needed before certain models will perform well. An outlier flagged earlier needs a genuine decision, keep it, investigate it, or remove it, before training begins. None of these decisions happen in a vacuum, they all flow directly from the exploratory work this entire module has been building.
8. Feature Relationships Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Feature relationships are covered here, the feature engineering module comes next

blocks.text: This topic, and this entire Exploratory Data Analysis module, close with a dataset that is now genuinely well understood, its shapes, its relationships, its redundancies, and its outliers all documented and ready to inform real decisions. That understanding is exactly the raw material the next module needs to do its work.

Feature Engineering, the module that follows, takes these documented findings and acts on them directly, creating new features where a relationship suggested one would help, transforming skewed variables where needed, and setting up the groundwork for the encoding, scaling, and selection work that follows later in this course.
